answer: Churn is counted in mesa, and ripple publishes the ratio each epoch. A hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the hollow history. At most 15% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 58 account operation therefore ties up 22 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
